8 cups (200g) fresh baby spinach or arugula

1 ripe mango, peeled, pitted, and diced

⅓ cup (35g) chopped walnut pieces

½ small red onion, sliced paper thin

FOR THE VINAIGRETTE: In a small blender or food processor, combine ⅓ cup (45g) of the blueberries with the vinegar, minced red onion, and pippali, then blend until smooth. Set aside.

FOR THE SALAD: In a large bowl, combine the spinach, mango, walnuts, red onion, and the remaining ⅔ cup (85g) of blueberries. Pour the dressing over the salad, toss to combine, and enjoy.

title: RAINBOW BROCCOLI SLAW
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 large head broccoli, about 12 ounces (340g)

1 large carrot, shredded

2 cups (190g) shredded purple cabbage

2 tablespoons minced scallion (green and white parts)

3 tablespoons sunflower seeds

¼ cup (35g) dried barberries, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes to soften

¼ cup (60ml) apple cider vinegar

2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

2 tablespoons chopped red onion

2 tablespoons almond butter

1 tablespoon Savory Spice Blend 2.0 (here)

1 tablespoon nutritional yeast

2 teaspoons white miso paste

1 teaspoon date sugar (optional)

1 tablespoon minced fresh parsley

1 teaspoon chopped fresh dill, or ½ teaspoon dried

FOR THE SLAW: Trim the ends of the broccoli stalks and cut off the florets. Reserve the broccoli florets for another use. Peel the broccoli stalks, then shred them in a food processor, using the large-hole shredding disk. Alternatively, halve the peeled stalks crosswise and thinly slice each half lengthwise to create rectangular slices. Cut the slices into matchsticks and transfer to a large bowl.

Add the carrot, cabbage, scallion, and sunflower seeds. Drain the barberries and add to the salad bowl. Toss to combine. Set aside.

FOR THE DRESSING: In a small blender or food processor, combine all the dressing ingredients, except the parsley and dill, and blend until smooth. Transfer the dressing to a bowl, then stir in the parsley and dill. Taste to adjust the seasonings, if needed, adding a little water if the dressing is too thick. Add as much of the dressing as needed to the slaw, stirring well to coat.

Set aside for 15 to 20 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to blend. If not serving right away, cover and refrigerate until ready to enjoy.

title: CUCUMBER SALAD WITH GRAPE TOMATOES
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

2 English cucumbers, thinly sliced

1 cup (75g) grape tomatoes, halved lengthwise

2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley or basil

1 tablespoon finely minced scallion or red onion (optional)

3 tablespoons rice vinegar

1 teaspoon white miso paste

Ground pippali or black pepper

Place the cucumber slices, tomatoes, and parsley or basil in a bowl. Add the scallion or red onion (if using). Set aside.

In a small bowl, combine the vinegar, miso paste, and pippali to taste, stirring to blend. Pour the dressing over the cucumbers and tomatoes, tossing gently to combine. Set aside for at least 10 minutes before serving, to allow the flavors to blend.

title: ROASTED CHICKPEA AND KALE SALAD WITH SWEET POTATOES AND APPLES
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1½ cups (370g) salt-free chickpeas, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

2 tablespoons dried barberries

1 pound (450g) sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch (1-cm) dice

6 cups (120g) coarsely chopped baby kale or arugula

¼ cup (60ml) balsamic or apple cider vinegar

1 tablespoon almond butter

1 tablespoon white miso paste

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

1 Fuji or Gala apple, or another crisp, sweet apple

½ cup (60g) chopped celery

¼ cup (25g) slivered almonds

2 scallions (green and white parts), minced

Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C). Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.

Pat the chickpeas dry with a paper towel and remove any loose skins. Spread the chickpeas in an even layer on the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, or until browned and crunchy, gently stirring them every 10 minutes or so to help them roast evenly. Watch the chickpeas closely for the last 10 minutes, so they do not burn. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool for 15 minutes.

Place the barberries in a small, heatproof bowl and cover with hot water. Set aside for 10 minutes to soften.

Steam the diced sweet potatoes in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot until just tender, 12 to 15 minutes.

Place the chopped kale in a large serving bowl. Add the cooked sweet potatoes and set aside.

In a small blender or food processor, combine the vinegar, almond butter, miso paste, and pippali. Blend until smooth. Set aside.

Core the apple, cut it into a ½-inch (1-cm) dice, and transfer to a small bowl. Pour the salad dressing onto the apple pieces and toss to coat. Add the apple mixture to the salad bowl with the kale and sweet potatoes. Drain the barberries and add them to the salad along with the celery, almonds, scallions, and chickpeas. Toss gently to combine and serve.

title: BARLEY SALAD WITH CREAMY TAHINI DRESSING
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 cup (180g) barley groats (hulled barley), rinsed well and drained

1½ cups (370g) salt-free white beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 cup (120g) finely chopped celery

1 large carrot, grated

3 scallions (green and white parts), minced

¼ cup (30g) dried goji berries, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes, then drained

½ cup (50g) pecan or walnut pieces, coarsely chopped

⅓ cup (13g) minced fresh parsley

3 tablespoons tahini

1 large garlic clove, crushed

2 tablespoons rice vinegar

1 tablespoon fresh lemon or lime juice

1 tablespoon nutritional yeast

2 teaspoons white miso paste

¼ teaspoon ground turmeric

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

FOR THE SALAD: In a saucepan, bring 3 cups (700ml) of water to a boil. Add the barley groats. Lower the heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer until the barley groats are tender but slightly chewy, 40 to 45 minutes. Drain well and place in a serving bowl. To the bowl, add the beans, celery, carrot, scallions, goji berries, pecans, and parsley, then set aside.

FOR THE DRESSING: In a small blender or food processor, combine the tahini, garlic, vinegar, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, miso paste, turmeric, pippali, and 2 tablespoons (30ml) of water. Blend until smooth, adding more water if needed, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the desired consistency is reached. Pour the dressing onto the salad, toss to combine, and serve.

title: THREE-BEAN SALAD WITH SPICY TOMATO DRESSING
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 6 TO 8 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1½ cups (375g) salt-free pinto beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1½ cups (375g) salt-free black beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1½ cups (400g) salt-free red kidney beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

1 cup (160g) fresh or thawed frozen corn kernels

2 tablespoons minced red onion

2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh cilantro

1 ripe avocado (optional)

3 plum tomatoes, cored and halved

2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar

2 tablespoons fresh lime juice

1 garlic clove, crushed

1 teaspoon minced jalapeño

2 teaspoons white miso paste

¼ teaspoon ground black cumin

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

FOR THE SALAD: In a large bowl, combine all the salad ingredients except the optional avocado, from pinto beans to cilantro, and set aside.

FOR THE DRESSING: In a blender or food processor, combine all the dressing ingredients, from tomatoes to pippali, and process until well blended.

Pour the dressing onto the salad and toss to combine. Taste to adjust the seasonings, if needed.

Cover and set aside for 30 minutes or refrigerate until ready to serve. When ready to enjoy, dice the avocado (if using) and add to the salad before serving.

title: SEAWEED SALAD WITH CUCUMBER
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

¼ cup (20g) dried cut wakame seaweed

3 tablespoons rice vinegar

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

1 tablespoon Umami Sauce 2.0 (here; optional)

1 tablespoon tahini

1 teaspoon white miso paste

3 small Persian cucumbers or 1 English cucumber

1 tablespoon sesame seeds

In a bowl, combine the wakame with 2 cups (470ml) of room-temperature water. Set aside for about 10 minutes to rehydrate.

In a separate medium bowl, combine the vinegar, lemon juice, Umami Sauce 2.0 (if using), tahini, and miso paste to make a dressing. Blend well, then set aside.

Cut off and discard the ends of the cucumbers. Cut the cucumbers in half, lengthwise, then cut them into thin half-moons. Place the sliced cucumbers in the bowl of dressing. Set aside.

Drain the wakame well, squeezing out any remaining water. If the wakame is not already in small pieces, place it on a cutting board and cut into 1⁄8-inch (3-mm) strips. Add the cut wakame to the bowl that contains the cucumber and dressing, and toss to combine.

When ready to serve, divide the salad among four small bowls and top with the sesame seeds. This salad is best served immediately or on the same day that it is made.

title: LENTIL–WALNUT BURGERS WITH CHEESY SAUCE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

⅓ cup (35g) chopped walnuts

⅓ cup (40g) chopped red onion

1 tablespoon ground flaxseeds mixed with 2 tablespoons warm water

2 tablespoons minced fresh parsley

1 tablespoon white miso paste

½ teaspoon onion powder

½ teaspoon garlic powder

¼ teaspoon paprika

¼ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

1 tablespoon Roasted Garlic (here; optional)

1½ cups (300g) cooked (not wet) brown lentils (see headnote)

½ cup (50g) rolled oats, or more as needed

Whole-grain burger buns or tortillas (optional)

Optional toppings: lettuce leaves, sliced tomato, sliced red onion

Cheesy Sauce (recipe follows)

FOR THE BURGERS: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Place a sheet of parchment paper on a rimmed baking sheet. Set aside.

In a food processor, combine the walnuts, red onion, flaxseed mixture, parsley, miso paste, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, sodium-free salt substitute (if using), and pippali. Pulse to combine, leaving some texture. Add the Roasted Garlic (if using), lentils, and oats. Pulse to mix together while leaving some texture. Pinch off a bit of the mixture and press it in your hand to make sure it holds together. If it’s too wet, add more oats; if it’s too dry, add some water, 1 tablespoon at a time. Taste to adjust the seasonings, if needed.

Shape the lentil mixture tightly into six burgers about ½-inch (1-cm) thick. Arrange them on the prepared baking sheet. Bake until golden brown, turning once, about 8 minutes per side.

TO SERVE: When the burgers are ready to serve, arrange them on a plate or on buns or tortillas (if using) along with any toppings you choose. Top with the Cheesy Sauce.

VARIATION: For Southwest Black Bean Burgers: Substitute black beans for the lentils, pepitas for the walnuts, and fresh cilantro for the parsley. Add 1 to 2 teaspoons of chili powder, ¼ cup (30g) of minced red bell pepper, and 2 tablespoons of chopped green onion, then proceed with the recipe.

MAKES: ABOUT 1 CUP (235ML) DIFFICULTY: EASY

½ cup (60g) raw cashews

3 tablespoons nutritional yeast

2 teaspoons white miso paste

1 teaspoon rice vinegar

⅛ teaspoon ground turmeric

1 teaspoon smoked paprika

In a small saucepan, combine the cashews with enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes. Drain the cashews, then transfer to a high-powered blender or food processor. Add ⅓ cup (80ml) of water and the nutritional yeast, miso paste, vinegar, turmeric, and paprika. Process until smooth. If the sauce is too thick, add more water, 1 tablespoon at a time. Store any leftover Cheesy Sauce in a container with a tight-fitting lid in the refrigerator for up to 1 week or freeze it for up to 3 months.

title: SPICY TEMPEH FAJITAS WITH RANCH DRESSING
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 (8-ounce) package (230g) tempeh

2 teaspoons chili powder

1 teaspoon smoked paprika

1 large red onion, halved lengthwise and thinly sliced

1 large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and thinly sliced

1 large yellow bell pepper, cored, seeded, and thinly sliced

1 medium zucchini, trimmed and cut into strips

2 garlic cloves, minced

½ teaspoon ground black cumin

½ teaspoon ground cumin

½ teaspoon ground coriander

¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper

4 large whole-grain tortillas

Ranch Dressing (recipe follows)

1 cup (25g) chopped or shredded greens, such as lettuce, cabbage, or kale

¼ cup (30g) sliced jalapeño

4 lime wedges

Steam the tempeh in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot for about 15 minutes. Cut the tempeh into thin strips. In a skillet, heat 2 tablespoons (30ml) of water over medium heat and add the tempeh strips. Sprinkle the tempeh with 1 teaspoon of the chili powder and ½ teaspoon of the paprika. Cook for about 2 minutes per side, turning as needed. Transfer the tempeh to a plate and return the pan to the stove.

Add about ¼ cup (60ml) of water to the same skillet and heat until hot. Add the red onion, bell peppers, zucchini, and garlic. Sauté for about 3 minutes, or until the vegetables soften. Add an extra tablespoon or two (15 to 30 ml) of water, if needed, so the vegetables don’t stick to the pan.

Add the tempeh strips, then stir in the remaining teaspoon of chili powder, remaining ½ teaspoon of paprika, and the black cumin, cumin, coriander, and cayenne. Continue to cook until the veggies are tender.

To serve, spoon the fajita filling in a line onto the bottom third of the tortillas. Roll up the tortillas, tucking in the sides. Top with the Ranch Dressing, chopped greens, and sliced jalapeño with the lime wedges on the side, and serve.

MAKES: ABOUT 1 CUP (235ML) DIFFICULTY: EASY

½ cup (60g) raw cashews

½ cup (120ml) unsweetened soy milk

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar

1 garlic clove, crushed

1 tablespoon chopped scallion

1 teaspoon white miso paste

½ teaspoon onion powder

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

In a small saucepan, combine the cashews and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes. Drain the cashews, then transfer them to a high-powered blender. Add the soy milk, lemon juice, vinegar, garlic, scallion, miso paste, onion powder, and pippali. Blend until smooth. Taste to adjust the seasoning, if needed. Transfer to a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes before using to allow the flavors to develop.

title: MUSHROOM–HUMMUS WRAPS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 large garlic clove

1½ cups (370g) salt-free chickpeas, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

3 tablespoons tahini

2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

1 teaspoon white miso paste

1 large red onion, halved lengthwise and cut into strips

1 large bell pepper (any color), cored, seeded, and thinly sliced

3 to 4 large portobello mushroom caps, cut into strips

¼ teaspoon ground black cumin

¼ teaspoon dried oregano

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

4 large whole-grain tortillas, warmed

Tomato Salsa (here), to serve (optional)

¼ cup (15g) chopped fresh cilantro

4 lime wedges, to serve

In a food processor, process the garlic until finely minced. Add the chickpeas and tahini, then process until smooth. Add the lemon juice, miso paste, and 3 tablespoons (45ml) of water. Process until well blended. If the hummus is too thick, add more water, 1 teaspoon at a time, and process to your desired consistency. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

In a large skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of water over medium-high heat. Add the red onion and bell pepper, then cook for about 2 minutes. Add the mushrooms, black cumin, oregano, and pippali. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes.

To serve, divide the hummus among the tortillas and spread it evenly onto each one. Divide the mushroom mixture on top of the hummus, about two-thirds of the way down the tortillas. Add a line of Tomato Salsa (if using) onto each tortilla, then top with cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice. Roll up the tortillas and serve.

title: GRILLED PORTOBELLO BURGERS WITH THE WORKS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

4 large portobello mushroom caps

8 slices large red onion

2 tablespoons Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

4 whole-grain burger buns

4 large lettuce leaves

4 slices large ripe tomato

1 large jalapeño, thinly sliced (optional)

Cheesy Sauce (here; optional)

Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C). On a parchment paper–lined baking sheet, arrange the mushroom caps and red onion slices in a single layer. Drizzle with Umami Sauce 2.0 and bake until browned on both sides, turning once, about 12 minutes per side.

Transfer the mushrooms and onion to a plate, and place the burger buns under the broiler, cut side up, until lightly toasted, about 5 minutes. Watch carefully so they don’t burn.

To serve, arrange a lettuce leaf and a tomato slice on the bottom half of each bun, then top each with a mushroom cap, two onion slices, and some jalapeño slices (if using). Drizzle with the Cheesy Sauce (if using) and cover with the top half of the bun. Serve hot.

title: LETTUCE WRAPS WITH MANGO SAUCE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
desc: MAKES: ABOUT 8 WRAPS (2 PER SERVING) DIFFICULTY: MODERATE
body:
MAKES: ABOUT 8 WRAPS (2 PER SERVING) DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 large ripe mango, peeled, pitted, and coarsely chopped

2 tablespoons rice vinegar

1 teaspoon white miso paste

½ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)

1 (8-ounce) package (230g) tempeh

1 cup (65g) chopped mushrooms

2 teaspoons grated ginger

½ medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

2 scallions (green and white parts), minced

2 tablespoons Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

1 ripe Hass avocado

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

8 large Boston or butter lettuce leaves

1 cup (110g) finely shredded carrot

⅓ cup (25g) chopped fresh cilantro

FOR THE MANGO SAUCE: In a blender or food processor, combine all the sauce ingredients and process until smooth. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

FOR THE LETTUCE WRAPS: Steam the tempeh in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot for about 15 minutes. Transfer the tempeh to a cutting board and chop into small, bite-sized pieces. In a skillet, heat 2 tablespoons (30ml) of water over medium heat. Add the tempeh, mushrooms, ginger, bell pepper, and scallions. Sauté for about 2 minutes. Add the Umami Sauce 2.0, stirring to coat. Cook for 1 minute longer, then remove from the heat and set aside.

Peel and pit the avocado. Cut the avocado into a small dice and place in a small bowl. Add the lemon juice and toss to coat the avocado.

Arrange the lettuce leaves on a large platter in a single layer, or place them on four individual plates, two leaves per serving. (The leaves should be face up to resemble cups for the filling.) Evenly top each lettuce leaf with the tempeh mixture, then add the diced avocado, carrot, and cilantro. Drizzle each lettuce cup with the Mango Sauce and serve any remaining sauce on the side. To eat, pick up a filled lettuce leaf and hold it as you would a taco.

title: BLACK BEAN BURRITOS WITH TOMATO SALSA
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 small red onion, minced [reserve 2 tablespoons for the Tomato Salsa (recipe below)]

1½ cups (375g) salt-free black beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

Tomato Salsa (recipe below)

1 cup (180g) cooked quinoa or other cooked whole grain or riced cauliflower

1 cup (160g) cooked fresh or frozen corn kernels

4 large whole-grain tortillas, warmed

Cheesy Sauce (here; optional)

In a saucepan, heat about ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, cover, and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the beans and about ½ cup (120ml) of Tomato Salsa and cook, stirring to combine. Simmer, mashing the beans as you stir them, until hot.

In a microwave-safe bowl, warm the quinoa and corn in a microwave, or heat in a small saucepan on the stovetop.

To serve, spoon about ½ cup (85g) of the bean mixture about two-thirds down each tortilla. Top each with ½ cup (90g) of the quinoa mixture and some Tomato Salsa. Drizzle with Cheesy Sauce (if using) before rolling up the burritos. Tuck in the sides of the burritos as you roll them up and serve hot.

MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

5 firm plum tomatoes, coarsely chopped

2 tablespoons minced red onion

1 jalapeño or another small hot chile, seeded and minced (optional)

1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar

2 tablespoons minced fresh cilantro or parsley

1 teaspoon white miso paste

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

In a bowl, combine all the ingredients and stir well. Cover and let stand at room temperature for an hour before serving. If not using right away, cover and refrigerate until needed.

title: SPICY POTATO AND SPINACH QUESADILLAS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

½ cup (60g) minced red onion

2 cups (130g) chopped mushrooms

2 garlic cloves, minced

½ teaspoon ground chipotle chile powder, or to taste

2 tablespoons white miso paste

8 cups (240g) baby spinach

2 large cooked russet potatoes, coarsely mashed

4 large whole-grain tortillas

Tomato Salsa (here; optional)

In a skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, cover, and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and garlic, then stir in the chipotle chile powder and miso paste. Cover and cook until the vegetables have softened, about 5 minutes. Add the spinach and cook, stirring, until it has wilted. Remove from the heat, draining off any liquid.

In a large bowl, combine the potatoes with the spinach mixture, stirring to mix well.

Divide the potato mixture among the tortillas, spreading it evenly over the bottom half of each tortilla. Fold the top half over the filling, pressing down lightly with your hands to enclose the filling. Arrange one or two of the quesadillas in a large skillet or on a griddle over medium-heat and cook until lightly browned on both sides, turning once. Keep them warm while you cook the remaining quesadillas. Repeat with the remaining ingredients. To serve, cut each quesadilla into three or four wedges and arrange on plates. Serve as is or with Tomato Salsa.

title: CURRIED TEMPEH WRAPS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 cup (120g) raw cashews

2 pitted dates

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

2 teaspoons curry powder, or to taste

1 teaspoon white miso paste

½ teaspoon onion powder

½ teaspoon garlic powder

1 (8-ounce) package (230g) tempeh

½ cup (50g) chopped walnuts

½ cup (50g) chopped apple

½ cup (55g) shredded carrot

¼ cup (30g) finely chopped celery

¼ cup (10g) finely chopped scallion (green and white parts)

¼ cup (30g) finely chopped red bell pepper

2 tablespoons minced fresh parsley

4 large whole-grain tortillas

2 to 3 cups (100 to 150g) shredded romaine lettuce

FOR THE CURRY DRESSING: In a small saucepan, combine the cashews, dates, and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes. Drain and rinse the cashews and dates, then transfer them to a high-powered blender. Add the lemon juice, curry powder, miso paste, onion powder, garlic powder, and ½ cup (120ml) of water. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add up to ¼ cup (60ml) more water, if needed, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the desired consistency is reached. (The dressing should be fairly thick.) Transfer to a bowl, cover, and refrigerate until needed.

FOR THE TEMPEH: Steam the tempeh in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot for about 10 minutes. Remove the tempeh from the saucepan and allow it to cool.

Pat the tempeh dry, chop it, and place it into a bowl. Add the walnuts, apple, carrot, celery, scallion, bell pepper, and parsley. Stir in about half of the Curry Dressing. Mix until thoroughly combined.

Stir in any remaining dressing, if desired, then cover the tempeh mixture and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes to allow the flavors to blend.

TO SERVE: To assemble, spread the tempeh mixture onto the tortillas, about two-thirds of the way down. Top with shredded lettuce and roll up. Cut each tortilla in half diagonally.

title: ROTINI WITH BROCCOLI AND CREAMY CAULIFLOWER SAUCE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

2½ cups (200g) cauliflower florets

1½ cups (375g) salt-free cannellini beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

3 to 4 garlic cloves, minced

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

1 tablespoon white miso paste

½ teaspoon dried basil

¼ teaspoon dried oregano

½ cup (120ml) unsweetened soy milk, or more as needed

8 ounces (225g) whole-grain rotini or other whole-grain pasta

4 cups (350g) small broccoli florets

2 tablespoons minced fresh parsley or basil, for garnish

Nutty Parm 2.0 (here), to serve (optional)

Steam the cauliflower in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot until tender, 6 to 8 minutes.

Drain the cauliflower and transfer to a blender or food processor. Add the beans, garlic, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, miso paste, basil, oregano, and soy milk. Process until smooth and well blended. Add more soy milk if the sauce is too thick, 1 tablespoon at a time. Set aside and keep warm.

In a large pot of boiling water, cook the rotini according to the package directions. About 5 minutes before the pasta is done cooking, add the broccoli.

Drain the pasta and broccoli well, then return to the pot. Add the cauliflower sauce and toss gently to combine and heat through. Serve hot, garnished with parsley or basil. Sprinkle Nutty Parm 2.0 (if using).

Variations: For a Soup: Steam the broccoli with the cauliflower and puree the vegetables with the other sauce ingredients to make a creamy crucifer soup, thinning out with soy milk as needed and to your taste.

For a Sauce: Instead of serving the sauce over pasta, spoon it over steamed or baked potatoes.

title: SPIRALIZED ZUCCHINI NOODLES WITH SPINACH–WALNUT PESTO
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

⅓ cup (35g) walnuts

2 large garlic cloves, chopped

5 cups (150g) packed chopped spinach

1 cup (30g) packed fresh basil leaves

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

2 teaspoons white miso paste

3 medium zucchini, ends trimmed

1 cup (150g) cherry or grape tomatoes, halved

1½ cups (375g) salt-free cannellini beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)

FOR THE PESTO: In a food processor, combine the walnuts and garlic, then pulse until finely ground. Add the spinach, basil, nutritional yeast, and miso paste. Pulse until finely chopped and well combined. Pour in ⅓ cup (80ml) of hot water and blend well. Set aside.

FOR THE ZUCCHINI NOODLES: Use a vegetable spiralizer or a julienne vegetable peeler to cut the zucchini into spirals or strands, respectively. In a large skillet, heat ½ cup (120ml) of water over medium-high heat. Working in batches if needed, add the zucchini noodles and cook until tender, about 3 minutes. Don’t overcook, or they will become too soft.

Immediately transfer the cooked zucchini to a large serving bowl. Add the tomatoes, beans, and pesto to the zucchini noodles and toss gently to combine. Serve warm, sprinkled with red pepper flakes (if using).

VARIATION: Use the pesto to top baked potatoes or toss with cooked whole-grain pasta.

title: BUCKWHEAT NOODLES WITH CABBAGE AND CREAMY CASHEW SAUCE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 pound (450g) Savoy cabbage, shredded

1 red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

2 garlic cloves, minced

6 fresh sage leaves, or ½ teaspoon dried or ground sage, plus more for garnish

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

8 ounces (225g) buckwheat noodles

1 cup (125g) frozen or fresh green peas

2 tablespoons white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

Creamy Cashew Sauce (recipe below)

¼ cup Nutty Parm 2.0 (here)

In a large skillet or pot, heat ½ cup (120ml) of water over medium heat. Add the cabbage, bell pepper, garlic, sage, and pippali. Cover and cook until the cabbage is tender, 15 to 20 minutes, stirring once about halfway through. Set aside.

In a large pot of boiling water, cook the noodles according to the package directions, adding the peas during the last 4 minutes of cooking time. Drain well and return the noodles and peas to the pot. Add the cabbage mixture and the miso mixture, then stir in the Creamy Cashew Sauce and simmer over low heat for a minute or two, stirring gently to heat and blend the flavors. Taste to adjust the seasonings as desired. Immediately serve hot, sprinkled with the Nutty Parm 2.0 and a few sage leaves for garnish.

MAKES: ABOUT 2 CUPS (475ML) DIFFICULTY: EASY

1¼ cups (150g) raw cashews

1 cup (235ml) unsweetened soy milk

1 tablespoon Roasted Garlic (here) or 2 garlic cloves, chopped

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

1 tablespoon white miso paste

2 teaspoons fresh lemon juice

In a small saucepan, combine the cashews and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes. Drain the cashews, then transfer them to a high-powered blender or food processor. Add the remaining ingredients. Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. If the sauce is too thick, add a little more soy milk, 1 tablespoon at a time.

The sauce is now ready to use in recipes or it can be transferred to a container, covered, and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: LASAGNA WITH KALE AND RED LENTIL TOMATO SAUCE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 cup (190g) red lentils, sorted and rinsed

6 cups (1.5L) salt-free marinara sauce, bottled or homemade

2 cups (160g) cauliflower florets

1½ cups (375g) salt-free cannellini beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

⅓ cup (25g) nutritional yeast

¼ cup (15g) minced fresh parsley

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

1 tablespoon white miso paste

1 teaspoon dried oregano

1 teaspoon dried basil

1 teaspoon garlic powder

1 teaspoon onion powder

½ teaspoon ground fennel seeds

¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

4 cups (85g) chopped kale, stems removed

12 whole-grain lasagna noodles

⅓ cup (45g) Nutty Parm 2.0 (here; optional)

FOR THE SAUCE: In a pot of boiling water, cook the lentils until soft, about 20 minutes for whole lentils or about 7 minutes for split lentils. Drain and return to the pot. Stir in the marinara sauce and simmer over low heat for about 5 minutes to incorporate the flavors. Set aside.

FOR THE FILLING: Steam the cauliflower in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot until soft, about 5 to 7 minutes, then transfer to a food processor. Add the beans and pulse until finely chopped.

Add the next ten ingredients. Process until well combined. Set aside.

Lightly steam the kale in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot until just tender, about 3 minutes. Set aside.

Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.

Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).

TO ASSEMBLE AND BAKE: Spread 1 cup (235ml) of the sauce on the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch (23 x 33-cm) baking dish. Top the sauce with a layer of noodles, then cover with half of the cauliflower and white bean filling. Top with more sauce and a layer of kale.

Repeat the layering process with the remaining ingredients, ending with a layer of noodles topped with sauce. Sprinkle with the Nutty Parm 2.0 (if using). Cover tightly and bake for 30 minutes, or until hot and bubbly. Remove from the oven, uncover, and let it stand for 10 minutes before cutting. Serve hot.

Variations: Use the Red Lentil Tomato Sauce over pasta. The cauliflower and white bean filling can be enjoyed as a spread for sandwiches or a delicious dip for crackers.

title: SPAGHETTI WITH MUSHROOM BOLOGNESE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 medium red onion, minced

1 medium carrot, minced

1 medium celery rib, minced

3 garlic cloves, minced

12 ounces (340g) fresh mushrooms, finely chopped

1 (28-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (800g) salt-free crushed tomatoes

2 tablespoons white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

1 teaspoon dried basil

½ teaspoon dried oregano

½ teaspoon ground fennel seeds

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

¼ cup (60ml) unsweetened soy milk

8 ounces (225g) whole-grain spaghetti

2 tablespoons minced fresh flat-leaf parsley

2 tablespoons Nutty Parm 2.0 (here; optional)

In a large saucepan, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cover and cook until tender, about 12 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding a little water if the vegetables begin to stick to the pan. Stir in the mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, miso mixture, nutritional yeast, basil, oregano, fennel seeds, and pippali. Simmer for 10 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender and any liquid is cooked down. Lower the heat to low and stir the soy milk into the sauce. Taste to adjust the seasonings as desired. Keep warm.

In a large pot of boiling water, cook the spaghetti according to the package directions. Drain well. Place the cooked pasta in a serving bowl, add the sauce, and toss gently to combine. Sprinkle with parsley and Nutty Parm 2.0 (if using). Serve hot.

title: WHITE BEAN MAC & CHEESE WITH GRAPE TOMATOES AND PEAS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

½ cup (60g) chopped yellow onion

1 large russet potato, peeled and chopped

1 large garlic clove, chopped

1½ cups (375g) salt-free cannellini beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 cup (235ml) Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

½ teaspoon ground turmeric

½ teaspoon onion powder

¾ teaspoon paprika

1 cup (235ml) unsweetened soy milk

⅓ cup (25g) nutritional yeast

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

8 ounces (225g) whole-grain elbow macaroni

1 cup (125g) frozen green peas, thawed

1 cup (150g) grape tomatoes, halved lengthwise

½ cup (60g) whole-grain bread crumbs

In a saucepan, heat ½ cup (120ml) of water over medium heat. Add the onion, potato, and garlic. Cover and cook until the vegetables are softened, about 10 minutes. Add the beans, Vegetable Broth 2.0, turmeric, onion powder, and ½ teaspoon of the paprika, then continue cooking until the vegetables are very soft. Remove from the heat.

In a high-powered blender or food processor, combine the vegetable mixture with the soy milk, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, and miso mixture, then blend until smooth. Taste to adjust the seasonings as desired. Set aside.

Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). In a pot of boiling water, cook the macaroni according to the package directions. About 5 minutes before the pasta is done cooking, add the peas to the pot. Drain and transfer the pasta and peas to a large baking dish.

Add the sauce to the cooked macaroni and peas in the baking dish. Fold in the tomatoes and spread the mixture evenly. Sprinkle the top with the bread crumbs and the remaining ¼ teaspoon of paprika. Bake until golden brown on top, about 20 minutes. Serve hot.

title: TAHINI SOBA NOODLES WITH BOK CHOY
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

3 tablespoons tahini

⅓ cup (80ml) Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

½ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)

1 large red onion, halved lengthwise and thinly sliced

3 cups (250g) shredded bok choy or napa cabbage

1 large carrot, thinly sliced

1 cup (80g) trimmed snow peas

2 teaspoons grated fresh ginger

8 ounces (225g) soba noodles

2 tablespoons sesame seeds

In a small blender or food processor, combine the tahini, Umami Sauce 2.0, lemon juice, ¾ cup (175ml) of water, and the red pepper flakes (if using). Set aside.

In a large skillet or wok, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium-high heat. Add the red onion, bok choy, and carrot, then stir-fry until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the snow peas, ginger, and, if needed, a little more water, then stir-fry for 2 more minutes. Set aside.

In a pot of boiling water, cook the soba noodles according to the package directions. Drain and transfer to a large bowl. Pour the tahini sauce and vegetables over the noodles and toss to combine. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and serve immediately.

title: SINGAPORE-STYLE NOODLES WITH TEMPEH
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 (8-ounce) package (230g) tempeh, cut into ½-inch (1-cm) dice

3 tablespoons Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

½ cup (130g) creamy peanut butter

2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

1½ teaspoons yellow curry powder, or more

¼ teaspoon ground cayenne

3 cups (250g) shredded napa cabbage or bok choy

1 large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

2 large garlic cloves, minced

½ cup (20g) chopped scallions (green and white parts)

2 teaspoons grated fresh ginger

8 ounces (225g) whole-grain angel hair pasta

1 cup (125g) frozen peas, thawed

¼ cup (32g) unsalted chopped peanuts

2 tablespoons minced fresh cilantro

Steam the tempeh in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot for about 10 minutes. Drain and transfer to a shallow bowl. Add the Umami Sauce 2.0 and set aside to marinate for about 10 minutes.

In a food processor, combine the peanut butter, ½ cup (120ml) of water, lemon juice, curry powder, and cayenne. Process until smooth, adding a little more water if the peanut sauce is too thick, 1 tablespoon at a time, then set aside.

In a large skillet or wok, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium-high heat. Add the cabbage, bell pepper, garlic, scallions, and ginger, then cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8 minutes. Lower the heat to low. Stir in the peanut sauce along with the tempeh and its marinade. Keep warm.

In a pot of boiling water, cook the pasta according to the package directions, adding the peas during the last 4 minutes of cooking time. Drain and transfer the pasta and peas to a large bowl.

Add the tempeh and vegetable mixture, then toss to combine. Serve topped with the peanuts and cilantro.

Variation: Instead of using tempeh, use soy curls. Simply soak 4 ounces (115g) of soy curls in a bowl of warm water to soften, then drain and squeeze out any remaining liquid. Transfer them to a shallow bowl, add Umami Sauce 2.0 (here) to marinate, then proceed with the recipe.

title: TOMATO PESTO PASTA WITH GREEN BEANS, CHICKPEAS, AND BELL PEPPERS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

3 large garlic cloves

⅓ cup (45g) pine nuts or slivered almonds

12 ounces (340g) Roma tomatoes, stem end removed, quartered lengthwise

1 cup (30g) packed fresh basil leaves

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

1 tablespoon white miso paste

8 ounces (225g) whole-grain pasta

8 ounces (225g) green beans, trimmed and cut into 1-inch (2.5-cm) pieces

1 large yellow bell pepper, cored, seeded, and cut into ½-inch (1-cm) pieces

1 small red or orange bell pepper, cored, seeded, and cut into ½-inch (1-cm) pieces

1½ cups (370g) salt-free chickpeas, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

Nutty Parm 2.0 (here), to serve (optional)

¼ to ½ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)

FOR THE PESTO: In a food processor, combine the garlic and pine nuts, then grind them into a paste. Add the remaining ingredients. Process, scraping down the sides as necessary, until the pesto is smooth. Transfer to a bowl, then add ⅓ cup (80ml) of hot water and stir to blend. Set aside.

FOR THE PASTA: In a large pot of boiling water, cook the pasta according to the package directions. About 5 minutes before the pasta is done cooking, add the green beans to the pot. About 3 minutes before the pasta is done cooking, stir in the bell peppers.

When the pasta and vegetables are cooked, drain them and return them to the pot. Add the chickpeas and pesto mixture, then toss gently to combine. Serve at once sprinkled with Nutty Parm 2.0 and red pepper flakes (if using).

title: VEGETABLE SHEET PAN SUPPER
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 pound (455g) beets, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5-cm) pieces

1 large red onion, halved lengthwise and sliced

1 pound (455g) purple or orange sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5-cm) pieces

1 large red bell pepper, halved, seeded, and sliced

8 ounces (225g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved

1½ cups (370g) salt-free chickpeas, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

3 garlic cloves, minced

3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

1 tablespoon nutritional yeast

1 teaspoon dried thyme

1 teaspoon dried oregano

1 teaspoon Savory Spice Blend 2.0 (here)

½ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

2 cups (300g) cherry tomatoes

¼ cup (15g) chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley or basil

¼ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C). Line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, combine the beets,* red onion, sweet potatoes, bell pepper, Brussels sprouts, and chickpeas. Add the garlic, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, thyme, oregano, Savory Spice Blend 2.0, and pippali. Toss to combine. Transfer the seasoned vegetables to the prepared pans and arrange them in a single layer.

Place the pans in the oven and roast the vegetables for 20 minutes. Remove the pans from the oven and stir the veggies. Distribute the tomatoes among the vegetables, then return the pans to the oven and roast for about 20 minutes longer, or until the vegetables are tender and the tomatoes have split open. Serve hot, sprinkled with the parsley and sodium-free salt substitute (if using).

* When beets are being prepared, their pink hue tends to get transferred to whatever they are cooked with. If you want to avoid this, roast the beets separately from other veggies.

title: KABOCHA SQUASH WITH BLACK RICE AND BEANS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
desc: MAKES: 4 SERVINGS (½ SQUASH PER SERVING) DIFFICULTY: MODERATE
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS (½ SQUASH PER SERVING) DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

¾ cup (135g) black rice

2 small kabocha squashes or other small winter squashes, halved* and seeded

⅓ cup (35g) walnut pieces

1 small red or yellow bell pepper, cored, seeded, and finely chopped

6 scallions (green and white parts), minced

2 garlic cloves, minced

2 teaspoons grated fresh ginger

1½ cups (375g) salt-free black beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

2 tablespoons Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

¼ cup (15g) minced fresh cilantro or parsley

½ teaspoon onion powder

¼ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

Balsamic Syrup (here), to serve (optional)

Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Rinse the rice. In a saucepan, combine the rice with 2 cups (470ml) of boiling water. Lower the heat to low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, about 40 minutes. Drain any remaining water. Set aside.

Place the squash halves, cut side down, in a shallow baking pan. Add ¼ inch (0.5cm) of water to the pan and cover tightly. Bake for 20 minutes, to soften slightly.

In a skillet, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the walnuts, bell pepper, scallions, garlic, and ginger, then cook, stirring, until fragrant and slightly softened, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl. Add the cooked rice, black beans, Umami Sauce 2.0, cilantro, onion powder, and sodium-free salt substitute (if using). Mix thoroughly to combine, then taste to adjust the seasonings, if desired.

Turn over the squash halves so they are cut side up, and fill the cavities with the stuffing, packing well. Cover and bake until the stuffing is hot and the squash is tender, 30 to 40 minutes. Serve hot, drizzled with Balsamic Syrup (if using).

* To make the squash easier to cut, microwave it for about 3 minutes, to soften slightly. Let it cool before cutting.

title: KALE AND MILLET–STUFFED BELL PEPPERS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 cup (180g) whole-grain millet, rinsed well and drained

1 medium red onion, minced

4 cups (85g) coarsely chopped kale, stems removed

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

¼ cup (35g) barberries, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes, then drained

2 tablespoons unsalted sunflower seeds

1 tablespoon ground flaxseeds

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

½ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

4 large red bell peppers, halved lengthwise and seeded

In a saucepan, bring 2 cups (500ml) of water to a boil. Add the millet, lower the heat to low, cover, and simmer until tender, about 25 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).

In a large skillet, heat ½ cup (120ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the kale and cook until tender, about 5 more minutes. Drain off any remaining liquid and set aside to cool.

Add the millet to the kale mixture in the skillet. Stir in the miso mixture, drained barberries, sunflower seeds, flaxseeds, nutritional yeast, pippali, and sodium-free salt substitute (if using). Mix well. Taste to adjust the seasonings, if needed.

Tightly pack the bell pepper halves with the millet stuffing and arrange them in a large shallow baking dish. Add about ½ cup (120ml) of water to the baking dish, cover tightly, and bake until the peppers are tender and the stuffing is hot, 30 to 40 minutes. Serve hot, two pepper halves per serving.

title: WINTER VEGETABLE STEW
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 cup (235ml) water or Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

1½ cups (180g) chopped red onion

1½ cups (165g) chopped carrots

1 large celery rib, chopped

2 garlic cloves, minced

1 or 2 teaspoons grated fresh ginger

¾ teaspoon onion powder

¾ teaspoon ground black cumin

½ teaspoon smoked paprika

¾ teaspoon dried thyme

2 slices fresh turmeric, or ¼ teaspoon ground turmeric powder

1 bay leaf

3 cups (330g) peeled and diced purple sweet potatoes

8 ounces (225g) green beans, trimmed and cut into 1-inch (2.5-cm) pieces

2 cups (45g) chopped kale, stems removed

1 (14.5-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (400g) salt-free diced tomatoes, undrained

1½ cups (370g) salt-free chickpeas, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

½ cup (65g) frozen peas

1 tablespoon white miso blended with ¼ cup (60ml) of hot water

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

¼ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

In a large pot, heat ½ cup (120ml) of the water over medium heat and bring to a simmer. Add the red onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cover and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the ginger, onion powder, black cumin, paprika, thyme, turmeric, and bay leaf. Cook, uncovered, while stirring, for 30 seconds. Add the sweet potatoes, green beans, kale, tomatoes in their juice, chickpeas, peas, and the remaining ½ cup (120ml) of water, then bring just to a boil. Lower the heat to low and simmer until the vegetables are tender, 35 to 40 minutes, adding a little more water, if needed.

Just before serving, stir in the miso mixture, pippali, and sodium-free salt substitute (if using). Remove the bay leaf and turmeric slices (if using). Taste to adjust the seasonings, if needed, and serve hot.

title: CABBAGE ROLLS STUFFED WITH BULGUR AND WHITE BEANS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 large green cabbage

1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped

1 small carrot, finely chopped

1 small red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and finely chopped

1 cup (140g) bulgur

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

1½ cups (365g) salt-free Great Northern white beans (or other small white beans), home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

2 tablespoons dried barberries, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes, then drained

1 tablespoon Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

¼ cup (15g) minced fresh parsley

½ teaspoon dried thyme

½ teaspoon garlic powder

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

½ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

2 cups (475ml) salt-free tomato sauce

1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar

1 teaspoon date sugar

½ teaspoon onion powder

Carefully remove 12 large leaves from the cabbage, reserving the remaining cabbage for another use. Steam the cabbage leaves in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot until softened, 8 to 10 minutes. Set aside to cool.

In a saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons (30ml) of water over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and bell pepper. Cover and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the bulgur and 1½ cups (350ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to low, stir in the miso mixture, and simmer until the bulgur has absorbed the water, about 15 minutes.

Transfer the bulgur mixture to a bowl. Add the beans, then stir in the drained barberries, Umami Sauce 2.0, parsley, thyme, garlic powder, pippali, lemon juice, and sodium-free salt substitute (if using). Mix well. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).

One at a time, place the cabbage leaves, rib side down, on a flat work surface. Press a small handful of the stuffing mixture in your palm so it holds together, then place it at the stem end of a cabbage leaf. Beginning at the stem end, roll up the leaf around the stuffing, tucking in the sides of the leaf as you roll it up. Repeat the process with the remaining softened leaves until the filling mixture is used up.

In a bowl, combine the tomato sauce with the balsamic vinegar, date sugar, and onion powder. Mix well. Pour half of the tomato sauce mixture into a 9 x 13-inch (23 x 33-cm) baking dish. Arrange the stuffed cabbage rolls, seam side down, in the baking dish. Pour the remaining sauce over the cabbage rolls. Cover tightly and bake until the cabbage is tender, about 45 minutes. Serve hot.

title: GRILLED VEGETABLE SKEWERS WITH UMAMI SAUCE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 large yellow bell pepper, cored, seeded, and cut into 1½-inch (4-cm) pieces

2 small zucchini, cut into 1-inch (2.5-cm) chunks

8 ounces (225g) fresh button or cremini mushrooms (halved lengthwise if large)

6 shallots, halved lengthwise

16 large cherry or Campari tomatoes

½ teaspoon onion powder

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

½ cup (120ml) Umami Sauce 2.0 (here), warmed

Thread the bell pepper, zucchini, mushrooms, shallots, and tomatoes onto eight wooden* or metal skewers, then arrange them in a shallow baking dish. Sprinkle with onion powder and pippali. Preheat a grill.

Place the skewered vegetables on a grill rack directly over the heat source. Grill until the vegetables are browned and tender, turning once halfway through, grilling for 10 to 15 minutes total. Transfer the skewers to a platter and drizzle them with Umami Sauce 2.0. Serve hot.

Variation: For Roasted Vegetable Skewers: If a grill is unavailable, you can roast the skewered vegetables in a 425°F (220°C) oven, on a parchment paper–lined rimmed baking sheet, for 20 to 30 minutes, turning once about halfway through.

* If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 1 hour before use to prevent burning.

title: ROASTED BUTTERNUT SQUASH WITH PINTO BEANS AND CORN
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 small butternut squash

1 medium red onion, chopped

1 medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

1½ cups (240g) fresh or frozen corn kernels

1 hot or mild chile pepper, seeded and minced

1½ cups (375g) salt-free pinto beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 cup (95g) shredded green cabbage

2 teaspoons Savory Spice Blend 2.0 (here)

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

2 tablespoons minced fresh cilantro or parsley

2 tablespoons pepitas

1 to 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice

1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar (optional)

Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C). Cut the squash in half, remove its seeds, and cut into ½-inch (1-cm) dice. Arrange the squash cubes, red onion, and bell pepper in a single layer in a 9 x 13-inch (23 x 33-cm) parchment paper–lined baking dish. Roast the vegetables in the oven until they are tender and slightly browned on the edges, about 30 minutes. Remove the baking dish from the oven and use a metal spatula to flip the vegetables. Stir in the corn and chile pepper. Return the pan to the oven and roast for another 10 minutes.

Once cooked, transfer the roasted veggies to a large serving bowl. Add the pinto beans, cabbage, Savory Spice Blend 2.0, pippali, cilantro, pepitas, lime juice, and balsamic vinegar (if using). Toss to combine. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: PINTO BEAN AND SWEET POTATO ENCHILADAS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

¼ cup (60ml) water or Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

1 medium red onion, chopped

1 large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

1 (15-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (400g) salt-free tomato sauce

1 tablespoon hot or mild chili powder, or to taste

1 teaspoon ground black cumin

½ teaspoon dried oregano

½ teaspoon garlic powder

½ teaspoon onion powder

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

¼ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

1 tablespoon white miso paste

1½ cups (375g) salt-free pinto beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 large sweet potato, cooked and chopped

1 teaspoon hot or mild chili powder

1 cup (165g) fresh or thawed frozen corn kernels

3 scallions (green and white parts), minced

¼ cup (30g) minced fresh cilantro

8 (8-inch/20-cm) whole-grain salt-free tortillas

Cheesy Sauce (here; optional)

FOR THE SAUCE: In a saucepan over medium heat, combine the water, red onion, and bell pepper, then cook, stirring, for 5 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender. Add the tomato sauce, chili powder, black cumin, oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, pippali, and sodium-free salt substitute (if using), and stir to blend. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove from the heat, stir in the miso paste, and set aside to cool slightly. Transfer the sauce mixture to a blender or food processor and process until smooth. Set aside.

FOR THE ENCHILADAS: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). In a bowl, combine the pinto beans, sweet potato, and chili powder. Coarsely mash together, then stir in the corn, scallions, and cilantro. Set aside.

To assemble, spread about ½ cup (120ml) of the sauce on the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch (23 x 33-cm) baking dish. Place one tortilla on a flat work surface and spoon about ⅓ cup (5 tablespoons) of the filling about two-thirds down the tortilla. Roll the tortilla closed and place it, seam side down, in the prepared baking dish. Repeat with the remaining tortillas, fitting the enchiladas snugly against each other. Pour the remaining sauce over enchiladas. Cover and bake until heated through, about 30 minutes. Before serving, spoon Cheesy Sauce (if using) over the enchiladas.

title: CHICKPEA AND BULGUR LOAF
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

¾ cup (90g) minced red onion

½ cup (55g) minced or grated carrot

½ cup (60g) minced celery

½ cup (35g) chopped mushrooms

2 garlic cloves, minced

½ cup (85g) bulgur

2 tablespoons ground flaxseeds

1 tablespoon white miso paste

1½ cups (370g) salt-free chickpeas, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

3 tablespoons nutritional yeast

2 tablespoons tomato paste

2 tablespoons chickpea flour

½ cup (60g) whole-grain bread crumbs

1½ teaspoons Savory Spice Blend 2.0 (here)

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

Umami Sauce 2.0 (here; optional)

In a saucepan, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, carrot, celery, mushrooms, and garlic. Cover and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the bulgur and 1 cup (235ml) of water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to low, cover, and simmer until the bulgur is tender and the water is absorbed, about 15 minutes. If any water remains, drain it off.

Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). In a small cup or bowl, combine the flaxseeds and miso paste with ¼ cup (60ml) of hot water. Stir to blend well, then set aside.

Place the chickpeas in a large bowl and mash well while leaving some texture. Add the cooked bulgur mixture to the bowl and stir in the flaxseed mixture. Add the nutritional yeast, tomato paste, chickpea flour, bread crumbs, Savory Spice Blend 2.0, and pippali. Mix well until thoroughly combined. Pinch off a small amount of the mixture to see whether it holds together. If it is too wet, mix in more bread crumbs.

Spoon the mixture into a parchment paper–lined loaf pan, pressing with your hands to make a smooth loaf. Spread some Umami Sauce 2.0 (if using) over the top of the loaf. Cover and bake until firm, 30 to 40 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes before turning out of the pan to a flat work surface to slice and serve.

title: SAMBAL-TOPPED SOY CURLS AND VEGETABLE STIR-FRY
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

1 or 2 hot red chile peppers, cored, seeded, and chopped

1 garlic clove, smashed

1 (½-inch/1-cm) piece fresh turmeric, grated, or ½ teaspoon ground turmeric

1 teaspoon white miso paste

1 teaspoon Date Syrup 2.0 (here) or date sugar

1 tablespoon rice vinegar

4 ounces (115g) soy curls

3 cups (250g) small broccoli florets

1 large red or yellow bell pepper, cored, seeded, and thinly sliced

8 ounces (225g) white mushrooms, sliced

2 garlic cloves, minced

3 tablespoons minced scallions (green and white parts)

1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger

FOR THE SAMBAL: In a skillet, combine the bell pepper, chile pepper, garlic, turmeric, miso paste, and Date Syrup 2.0 over medium heat. Stir in ⅓ cup (80ml) of water and cook for about 5 minutes to soften. Transfer the mixture to a blender or food processor, add the vinegar, and blend until smooth. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside to cool to room temperature.

FOR THE STIR-FRY: In a bowl, combine the soy curls with enough warm water to cover. Let them soak for 10 minutes to soften, then drain and squeeze out any remaining liquid. Set aside.

Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add 2 tablespoons of water. Add the broccoli, bell pepper, and mushrooms, then stir-fry until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the soy curls, garlic, scallions, and ginger. Stir-fry for about 3 minutes, then stir in the sambal mixture. Continue to stir-fry until the soy curls and vegetables are hot and well coated with the sambal, adding a little more water if needed. Serve hot.

title: RED BEAN AND TEMPEH JAMBALAYA
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 (8-ounce) package (230g) tempeh

1 medium red onion, chopped

2 celery ribs, chopped

1 medium green bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

2 garlic cloves, minced

3 cups (810g) salt-free dark red kidney beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 (14.5-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (400g) salt-free diced tomatoes, drained

1 (14.5-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (400g) salt-free crushed tomatoes, undrained

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

1 teaspoon dried thyme

½ teaspoon dried marjoram

2 tablespoons Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

½ teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste

¼ teaspoon ground cayenne, or to taste

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

1 teaspoon filé powder (optional)

3 cups (600g) cooked brown rice or other favorite cooked whole grain

1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley

Steam the tempeh in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot for about 10 minutes. Remove from the heat, then transfer the tempeh to a flat work surface and cut it into a ½-inch (1-cm) dice. Set aside.

In a large pot, heat ½ cup (120ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, celery, bell pepper, and garlic. Cover and cook until softened, about 8 minutes. Stir in the diced tempeh and cook 5 minutes longer.

Add the beans, diced tomatoes, crushed tomatoes in their juice, miso mixture, thyme, marjoram, Umami Sauce 2.0, red pepper flakes, cayenne, pippali, and filé powder (if using). Cover and simmer until the vegetables are soft, about 20 minutes. Stir in the cooked rice and cook, uncovered, for 5 to 10 minutes longer. Serve hot, sprinkled with parsley.

title: BLACK BEAN STEW WITH PURPLE SWEET POTATOES
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 large red onion, chopped

2 garlic cloves, minced

2 large purple sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch (1-cm) dice (about 4 cups/440g diced)

1 medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and diced

1 small jalapeño, seeded and minced (optional)

2 cups (470ml) Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here) or water

3 cups (750g) salt-free black beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 (14.5-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (400g) salt-free diced tomatoes, undrained

2 teaspoons white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

1 ripe mango, peeled, pitted, and diced

½ cup (30g) chopped fresh cilantro

In a large pot, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, then cover and cook until softened, stirring occasionally, about 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook another 2 minutes. Add a little more water, if needed, to prevent the onion and garlic from sticking to the bottom of the pot.

Add the sweet potato, bell pepper, jalapeño (if using), and Vegetable Broth 2.0. Bring to a boil. Lower the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the sweet potatoes are tender but still firm, about 25 minutes.

Stir in the beans, tomatoes in their juice, and miso mixture, then simmer gently, uncovered, until heated through, about 5 minutes. Add the mango and cook for 1 more minute, then stir in the cilantro and serve hot.

title: TEMPEH SATAY WITH SPICY PEANUT SAUCE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 garlic clove, chopped

3 tablespoons peanut butter

1 tablespoon rice vinegar

2 teaspoons white miso paste

¼ teaspoon ground cayenne, or to taste

1 (8-ounce) package (230g) tempeh

1 tablespoon Date Syrup 2.0 (here)

1 tablespoon white miso paste

1½ tablespoons grated fresh ginger

2 tablespoons fresh lime juice

2 tablespoons rice vinegar

1 garlic clove, minced

½ teaspoon ground coriander

½ teaspoon ground black cumin

½ teaspoon ground turmeric

Shredded lettuce (or cooked grains and dark leafy greens)

Lime wedges

Cilantro sprigs

FOR THE PEANUT SAUCE: In a small blender or food processor, combine the garlic, peanut butter, vinegar, and miso paste, then blend to a paste. Add the cayenne and ⅓ cup (80ml) of water, and blend until smooth. If the sauce is too thick, blend in a little more water. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside. If not using the sauce right away, cover and refrigerate until needed.

FOR THE TEMPEH AND MARINADE: Cut the tempeh into 1-inch (2.5-cm) cubes. Steam the tempeh in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot for 10 minutes, then drain, transfer to a shallow bowl, and set aside.

In a small bowl, combine the Date Syrup 2.0, miso paste, ginger, lime juice, vinegar, garlic, coriander, black cumin, and turmeric, then set aside.

Thread the tempeh onto skewers and arrange them in a single layer in a baking pan. Pour the marinade over the tempeh, turning to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature or up to two hours in the refrigerator.

Preheat the grill or broiler. Remove the tempeh skewers from the pan and reserve the marinade. Place the skewers on a hot grill or under the broiler until browned, about 5 minutes per side.

TO SERVE: Spread shredded lettuce (or cooked grains and greens) on a platter. Arrange the tempeh skewers on top. Drizzle with the marinade and garnish with the lime wedges and cilantro. Serve with the Spicy Peanut Sauce.

title: RED LENTIL PATTIES WITH MUSHROOM GRAVY
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 cup (190g) red lentils

1 small red onion, finely chopped

2 garlic cloves, minced

2 tablespoons ground flaxseeds

1 tablespoon white miso paste

⅓ cup (30g) chickpea flour

⅔ cup (80g) whole-grain bread crumbs

⅓ cup (25g) nutritional yeast

3 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley

1 tablespoon tomato paste

1 teaspoon dried thyme

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

¼ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

Mushroom Gravy (recipe below; optional)

In a saucepan, combine the lentils with 2 cups (470ml) of water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to low, stir in the red onion and garlic, cover, and simmer until tender, about 8 minutes. If any water remains, drain well and set the lentils aside. Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.

In a small cup or bowl, combine the flaxseeds and miso paste with 2 tablespoons of hot water, stirring to blend well. Set aside for 2 to 3 minutes to thicken.

Transfer the cooked lentil mixture to a bowl. Add the flaxseed mixture. Stir in the chickpea flour, bread crumbs, nutritional yeast, parsley, tomato paste, thyme, pippali, and sodium-free salt substitute (if using). Mix until all the ingredients are well combined. Pinch off a small amount of the mixture to check that it holds together well. If the mixture is too loose, mix in more bread crumbs.

Use your hands to divide the mixture equally into six balls. Flatten each ball into a patty and arrange them on the prepared baking sheet. Bake until firm and lightly browned on both sides, 15 to 20 minutes, turning once about halfway through. Serve topped with the Mushroom Gravy (if using).

MAKES: ABOUT 3 CUPS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1½ cups (350ml) Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

1 small yellow onion, finely chopped

8 ounces (225g) cremini mushrooms, thinly sliced

3 garlic cloves, minced

2 tablespoons oat flour

½ cup (120ml) unsweetened soy milk

2 tablespoons Umami Sauce 2.0 (here)

¾ teaspoon dried thyme

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add ¼ cup (60ml) of the Vegetable Broth 2.0 and the onion, and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and garlic. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has almost evaporated, about 5 minutes. Sprinkle in the oat flour and continue stirring until it has been absorbed. Add the remaining 1¼ cups (290ml) of Vegetable Broth 2.0, stirring until incorporated, and continue to cook until the liquid has thickened. Stir in the soy milk, Umami Sauce 2.0, thyme, and pippali. Continue to simmer over medium-low heat until thickened, stirring frequently. Serve hot. If not serving right away, set aside to cool, then cover and refrigerate until needed.

title: WHITE BEAN CASSOULET
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 medium red onion, chopped

2 large carrots, chopped

1 celery rib, chopped

3 garlic cloves, minced

3 cups (740g) salt-free Great Northern beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1½ cups (375g) salt-free cannellini beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 (14.5-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (400g) salt-free crushed tomatoes, undrained

1 tablespoon minced fresh parsley

1 teaspoon dried thyme

1 teaspoon dried savory

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with ½ cup (120ml) hot water or Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

½ cup (60g) whole-grain bread crumbs

Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). In a large skillet, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cover and cook until softened, about 10 minutes.

Transfer the vegetables to a 2½ to 3-quart (2.5 to 3-L) baking dish. Stir in all the beans, tomatoes in their juice, parsley, thyme, savory, pippali, and the miso mixture.

Cover tightly and bake for 45 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender and the flavors have blended.

Remove the cassoulet from the oven, uncover, and top with the bread crumbs. Return the baking dish to the oven, uncovered, and bake for 10 more minutes to lightly brown the bread crumbs. Serve hot.

title: TEMPEH AND MUSHROOM CHILI WITH CORN AND CILANTRO
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 (8-ounce) package (230g) tempeh

1 medium red onion, chopped

1 medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

3 garlic cloves, minced

8 ounces (225g) cremini mushrooms, chopped

2 to 3 tablespoons chili powder (mild or hot)

½ teaspoon dried oregano

½ teaspoon ground black cumin

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

2 (14.5-ounce) BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks (800g) salt-free crushed tomatoes, drained

3 cups (810g) salt-free dark red kidney beans, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

1 cup (160g) fresh or thawed frozen corn kernels

½ cup (30g) chopped fresh cilantro

Steam the tempeh in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot for 10 minutes. Drain, coarsely chop, and set aside.

In a large saucepan, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion and bell pepper, cover, and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.

Add the miso mixture and garlic, then stir in the tempeh, mushrooms, chili powder, oregano, black cumin, and pippali. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, beans, and corn.

Cover and simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the chili is thick and flavorful, about 30 minutes. Stir in the cilantro. If the chili is too thick, stir in a little water. Serve hot.

title: TWO-LENTIL DAL
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

¾ cup (145g) green lentils, well rinsed

¾ cup (130g) brown lentils, well rinsed

4¼ cups (1L) water or Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

1 medium red onion, minced

2 garlic cloves, minced

2 teaspoons grated fresh ginger

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with 2 tablespoons hot water

1 tablespoon curry powder

½ teaspoon ground black cumin

½ teaspoon ground coriander

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

1 (14.5-ounce) BPA-free can or Tetra Pak (400g) salt-free crushed tomatoes

½ teaspoon ground fenugreek seeds (optional)

In a large saucepan, combine the green and brown lentils with 4 cups (940ml) of the water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium and simmer gently for about 30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Set aside.

In a skillet, heat the remaining ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the red onion, cover, and cook until soft, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger, and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in the miso mixture, curry powder, black cumin, coriander, pippali, tomatoes, and fenugreek (if using), stirring constantly for about 1 minute. Add the tomato mixture to the lentils and stir to mix well. Simmer gently over low heat for about 5 minutes to allow the flavors to blend and the dal to thicken. Taste to adjust the seasonings before serving.

title: MILLET AND CAULIFLOWER–TOPPED SHEPHERD’S PIE
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: MODERATE

1 cup (180g) millet, soaked in water for 8 hours or overnight

2½ cups (600ml) water or Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

3 cups (285g) finely chopped or grated cauliﬂower

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with 2 tablespoons hot water

1 tablespoon nutritional yeast

½ teaspoon onion powder

1¼ cups (300ml) water or Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

½ cup (90g) brown or green lentils

1 tablespoon white miso paste

2 teaspoons tomato paste

1 large red onion, chopped

2 large carrots, chopped

2 garlic cloves, minced

2 cups (130g) chopped mushrooms

1 cup (160g) fresh or thawed frozen corn kernels

1 cup (125g) fresh or thawed frozen peas

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

1 teaspoon dried thyme

1 teaspoon dried marjoram

1 teaspoon onion powder

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

¼ teaspoon smoked paprika

FOR THE TOPPING: Drain the soaked millet and rinse well. Transfer the millet to a large saucepan, add the water, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to medium. Cover and simmer for about 15 minutes, then stir in the cauliflower and continue to cook for 5 to 7 minutes, or until the millet and cauliflower are soft and the water is absorbed. Drain off any remaining liquid. Add the miso mixture, nutritional yeast, and onion powder, and use a potato masher to mash the mixture together. Taste to adjust the seasonings, if needed, adding a little more nutritional yeast, if desired. Set aside. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).

FOR THE FILLING: In a saucepan, combine 1 cup (235ml) of the water and the lentils, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender. Remove from the heat. In a small bowl or cup, combine the miso paste, tomato paste, and 2 tablespoons of water. Stir to blend well. Stir the miso mixture into the lentils and set aside.

In a skillet, heat the remaining ¼ cup (60ml) of the water over medium heat. Add the red onion, carrot, and garlic, then stir in the mushrooms, corn, and peas. Cover and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Uncover, stir in the nutritional yeast, thyme, marjoram, onion powder, and pippali. Continue to cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes longer. Combine the cooked lentils with the vegetables, and taste to adjust the seasonings, if needed.

TO ASSEMBLE: Spread the lentil filling evenly in a 9 x 13-inch (22 x 33-cm) baking dish. Spoon on the millet and cauliflower topping, spread it evenly, and sprinkle with the paprika. Bake until hot, about 30 minutes. Serve hot.

title: TURMERIC QUINOA WITH BROCCOLI, CHICKPEAS, AND TOMATOES
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 TO 6 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1¾ cups (410ml) water or Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here)

1 small red onion, minced

1 cup (180g) quinoa, rinsed well and drained

½ teaspoon ground turmeric

2 teaspoons white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

3 cups (250g) small broccoli florets

1½ cups (370g) salt-free chickpeas, home-cooked or from BPA-free cans or Tetra Paks, drained and rinsed

2 teaspoons Roasted Garlic (here)

2 tablespoons nutritional yeast

½ teaspoon onion powder

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

1½ cups (225g) grape tomatoes, halved lengthwise

In a saucepan, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of the water over medium heat. Add the red onion, cover, and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the quinoa and turmeric, then add the remaining 1½ cups (350ml) of water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to low.

Stir the miso mixture into the pot of quinoa. Cover and simmer until the quinoa has absorbed all of the water, 15 to 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, steam the broccoli in a metal steamer basket over an inch (2.5cm) or so of boiling water in a covered saucepan or pot until it is just tender, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, uncover, and set aside.

Transfer the cooked quinoa to a serving bowl and stir in the chickpeas. Add the Roasted Garlic, nutritional yeast, onion powder, pippali, tomatoes, and the steamed broccoli. Toss gently to combine, then serve.

title: BARLEY RISOTTO WITH ARTICHOKES AND MUSHROOMS
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 (10 to 12-ounce) package (280 to 340g) frozen artichoke hearts, thawed and chopped

8 ounces (225g) mushrooms, sliced

3 garlic cloves, minced

1 cup (185g) barley, rinsed well and drained

1 tablespoon white miso paste blended with ¼ cup (60ml) hot water

1 teaspoon Savory Spice Blend 2.0 (here)

1 teaspoon minced fresh thyme, or ¼ teaspoon dried

½ teaspoon onion powder

¼ teaspoon ground pippali or black pepper

3½ cups (825ml) Vegetable Broth 2.0 (here), or more as needed

¼ teaspoon sodium-free salt substitute (optional)

In a large saucepan, heat ¼ cup (60ml) of water over medium heat. Add the artichokes, mushrooms, and garlic. Cover and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the barley, miso mixture, Savory Spice Blend 2.0, thyme, onion powder, pippali, ½ cup (120ml) of the Vegetable Broth 2.0, and sodium-free salt substitute (if using), and simmer, stirring gently, until the liquid is absorbed.

Add the remaining broth, 1 cup (235ml) at a time, stirring until the liquid is absorbed before each addition. Simmer, stirring frequently, until your desired consistency is reached, adding a bit more liquid, if needed, until the barley is tender. Serve hot.

title: SORGHUM WITH CORN AND ARUGULA
book: The How Not to Age Cookbook
author: Michael Greger
body:
MAKES: 4 SERVINGS DIFFICULTY: EASY

1 cup (190g) whole-grain sorghum, soaked in water for 8 hours or overnight
