desc: COOK TIME: 30 MINUTES, PLUS 1 HOUR CHILL TIME MAKES 4 PIES
body:
COOK TIME: 30 MINUTES, PLUS 1 HOUR CHILL TIME MAKES 4 PIES

There’s nothing more American than apple pie. And now you can have a Blue Zones–approved version in the form of these portable pies wrapped in a flaky crust and filled with warm and comforting apple and cinnamon.

FOR THE CRUST

1 cup whole wheat pastry flour

½ cup fine semolina flour

4 ounces coconut oil, frozen and cut into chunks

Pinch of salt

¼ cup ice water

FOR THE FILLING

1 large pie apple, finely diced

2 tablespoons raisins

½ teaspoon cornstarch

2 tablespoons maple syrup, plus 2 tablespoons to finish

¼ teaspoon cinnamon

To make the crust, put the flours, coconut oil, and salt in a food processor and pulse until the oil is broken up, with the largest pieces no bigger than a pea.

Add the water and pulse again until the dough starts to come together. Don’t overwork it or it will get tough. Turn the dough out onto your work surface, gather it into a ball, and wrap it tightly. Rest it in the fridge for at least an hour or up to overnight.

To make the filling, toss all the ingredients (except the maple syrup for finishing) in a bowl until combined.

Preheat your oven to 375°F.

To make the hand pies, let the dough come to room temperature. Lightly flour your work surface and roll the dough out into a sheet about ⅛ inch thick. Use a knife to trim ragged edges, then use the trimmed pieces and press to fill any holes so that you end up with a rectangle about 12 inches wide and 16 inches long.

Cut the sheet of dough into rectangular quarters. Place a quarter of the filling on one half of each piece of dough, leaving ½ inch around the edges. Fold the empty half of the dough over the filling, line up the edges, and press down gently all the way around. Use a fork to poke the top of each pie and then press down with the fork to seal the three joined edges of the crust.

Brush the tops of the pies with the remaining maple syrup and bake for 30 minutes.

You can make the crust ahead of time and keep it tightly wrapped in the fridge overnight or in the freezer for up to a month.

title: Brûlée Pears With Spiced Yogurt & Muesli
book: The Blue Zones Kitchen One Pot Meals
author: Dan Buettner
body:
COOK TIME: 5 MINUTES MAKES 4 SERVINGS

When they’re perfectly ripe, pears have an almost tropical aroma that melds beautifully with cardamom. Broiling them with a bit of sugar deepens their flavor, and cooling yogurt and our toasty Muesli add a satisfying and nutritious treat.

½ cup Muesli (see here, or store-bought)

1 cup unsweetened coconut milk yogurt alternative

¼ teaspoon ground cardamom

¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon

2 ripe pears, halved lengthwise and cored

1 teaspoon coconut sugar

Fresh mint sprigs, for garnish

Set your oven to broil on high.

In a shallow ovenproof pan big enough to hold all the pear halves, toast the muesli over medium-high heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Place the muesli into a small bowl and set aside.

Meanwhile, combine the yogurt and spices in a small bowl; mix well and set aside.

Put the pears in the pan, cut side up, and sprinkle with the sugar. Broil the pears until the sugar browns and caramelizes, about 3 to 5 minutes.

To serve, put ¼ cup of spiced yogurt on each plate, set a pear on top of the yogurt, and sprinkle some muesli over the pear. Garnish with a mint sprig.

title: Mulled Cider Tonic
book: The Blue Zones Kitchen One Pot Meals
author: Dan Buettner
desc: COOK TIME: 15 MINUTES MAKES ABOUT 4 (1-CUP) SERVINGS
body:
COOK TIME: 15 MINUTES MAKES ABOUT 4 (1-CUP) SERVINGS

For another cozy recipe, turn to mulled cider—a classic fall treat. This version reduces the sugar but boosts the flavor, adding orange, spicy fresh ginger, and tangy cider vinegar for a nourishing drink that’s great hot or cold. If you want to turn this into a wonderful post-exercise refresher, add a pinch of sea salt.

1 orange, halved and juiced, rind reserved

2 cups apple cider

2 cups water

2 apples, cored and chopped into roughly ½-inch pieces

2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar

10 cardamom seeds (or 2 pods)

6 allspice berries

4 cloves

1 cinnamon stick

1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated

¼ teaspoon grated nutmeg

Orange slices, for garnish

Cinnamon sticks, for garnish

Put all the ingredients except the garnishes in a saucepan (including the orange rind; you want the flavor from the peel) and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Lower the heat to a simmer and let the mixture cook until the apple chunks are soft, about 15 minutes.

Pour the mixture through a strainer, pushing on the apple chunks with the back of a spoon to extract as much liquid as you can.

Serve garnished with an orange slice and cinnamon stick (if using). You can store any remaining cider in the fridge for up to a week.
